parsed.explanation: No trans-specific law, incident, entry, facility or custody evidence is documented, so the rating extrapolates thinly from the surrounding regime. Same-sex conduct is regularly prosecuted in government areas at 3 months-3 years, with post-sentence surveillance, while death is reported and imposed under sharia in insurgent/southern areas and armed groups executed men in 2024. Severe taboo and stigma, no anti-discrimination protection, civil war and general impunity mean no documented recourse if a visibly trans visitor is outed and treated as a morality/sexual-conduct offender. Execution is not documented for trans presentation, keeping it above the 0.05 tier, but the combined regime makes imprisonment and lethal non-state violence credible.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Regular prosecutions for same-sex conduct in government areas, 3 months-3 years, plus Article 410 police surveillance; no trans-specific custody documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing could be pursued as a morality/sexual-conduct offence, with surveillance extending exposure after release.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Two regimes: short civil prison terms in government-controlled areas; capital punishment at judicial discretion in insurgent-controlled and southern areas.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The operative penalty depends on control line, so a visitor cannot rely on the civil regime everywhere in the country.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Same-sex conduct criminalised with irreconcilable penalties up to life/death in sources; regular prosecution, severe stigma and taboo, no discrimination prohibition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No known official executions reported for 2022, but impunity was the norm.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality law is secondary for trans visitors, but here it is actively enforced and paired with stigma and no recourse.

minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented; no age-dependent rule is sourced, so no guardian-specific exposure is inferred.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Non-state armed groups killed men alleged to have engaged in homosexual activity in 2017, 2018 and executed two men in 2024; pervasive violence and impunity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw counts have no denominator and are not trans-specific, but they show lethal enforcement by armed actors against perceived sexual nonconformity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no public discussion, severe stigma, thin discreet organisations, and no documented effective remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse applies also to the trans-specific unknowns: entry, documents, facilities and care are unsourced, not answered.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.05: execution for trans presentation, lethal custody and vanishing appeals are not documented here, and government reports found no known official executions of the relevant kind, so the lethal pathway is less directly established.

Similar to 0.15 but slightly higher: routine prosecution, possible capital punishment in parts of the country, impunity and no remedy align, while documented trans-specific arrest, beatings in custody and months-long pretrial detention are absent.

Lower than 0.25: unlike short jail terms with no execution, this dossier documents regular prosecution plus capital punishment imposed in insurgent/southern areas and armed-group executions as recently as 2024, raising severity if outed.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a functioning dual system: civil imprisonment in government areas and possible death elsewhere, enforced sporadically amid war and impunity. Trans-specific exposure is unsourced, so sexuality law should not dominate alone, but regular prosecution, lethal armed-group enforcement, severe stigma and zero documented recourse make outing potentially catastrophic. No protective operative regime for visitors is documented at entry, in facilities, in care or in custody.
